disposition_mapping.rationale: Issuance of the calendar and central planning assumptions, including the mandatory downside macro scenario, is preserved substantially unchanged; the only change is the addition of a scenario-modelling tool to build the downside variant.

Unconstrained by design. Top-down target setting is reorganised to explicitly produce base and downside target variants, consistent with the scenario set now issued upstream, improving resilience planning without changing the governing actors.

Revenue and volume planning is preserved as a distinct business-unit-owned activity but reorganised onto a shared driver-based planning platform with automated actuals/driver feeds to reduce manual assumption re-entry.
Cost centre and headcount budgeting is preserved as a distinct cost-centre-owned activity but reorganised onto the shared driver-based platform with automated headcount cost calculation.
Capex request submission is preserved but reorganised into an automated workflow that still mandatorily consumes a business case for requests above threshold, now with ROI scoring attached.

Consolidation into the draft three-statement budget is preserved but reorganised around an automated consolidation engine that still consumes the accounting policies applied to actuals and the central FX assumptions, and now also produces a reconciliation report as a formal output.

Unconstrained by design. Review and challenge iterations are preserved but reorganised to be driven by automated variance flags from the reconciliation report, focusing CFO/FP&A challenge effort on material outliers.
Board approval is preserved unchanged as the governance gate before the budget is locked.

Loading and locking of the approved version is preserved, occurring after board approval, now explicitly tied to an EPM platform with an audit trail, maintaining it as the single version used by variance analysis.

steps.description: FP&A issues the budget calendar and central planning assumptions (inflation, FX, interest rates) together with at least one downside macro scenario, built using an integrated scenario-modelling tool so that base and downside variants are available to all submitters from day one.
steps.name: Issue calendar, central planning assumptions and scenario set

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets, modelled against both the base case and the downside scenario so submitters receive explicit base and contingency targets.
steps.name: Set top-down targets (scenario-adjusted)

steps.description: Business unit heads prepare and own revenue and volume plans in a shared planning platform, with drivers and actuals fed in automatically to reduce manual reconciliation of assumptions.
steps.name: Driver-based revenue and volume planning

steps.description: Cost centre owners prepare and own cost centre and headcount budgets in the shared planning platform, with headcount cost calculations automated from driver libraries (e.g. salary bands, FTE counts).
steps.name: Driver-based cost centre and headcount planning

steps.description: Business unit heads submit capex requests through an automated workflow that mandatorily attaches and routes a business case, with ROI scoring, for any request above the materiality threshold.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests with automated business case workflow

steps.description: Submissions are consolidated automatically into a draft three-statement budget prepared on the same accounting basis as actuals, applying central FX assumptions and the accounting policies applied to actuals, with the three statements reconciled by the system and variance flags raised for policy or FX inconsistencies.
steps.name: Automated consolidation and reconciliation into draft three-statement budget

steps.description: The draft budget is reviewed and challenged in iterative cycles with submitters, with automated variance flags and dashboards directing challenge effort to material outliers rather than uniform line-by-line review.
steps.name: Continuous, data-driven review and challenge

steps.description: The board reviews and approves the final budget, including the embedded downside scenario view.
steps.name: Board approval

steps.description: The board-approved budget is loaded into the EPM/FP&A platform and locked as the single immutable version used by variance analysis, with a full audit trail of the load.
steps.name: Load and lock approved version in EPM platform
